files.lang.knl:
(* Kanon's built-in bool module, which [use builtin "bool"] reads: here
   bool.knl and bool.kn are copies of it, which [use "bool"] uses, to read and
   to edit. *)

[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "bool"
files.bool.knl:
(* The bool module, at the bottom of every language: booleans, equality, [Ite]
   and [Distinct]. See the reference of Kanon for the syntax. It is proved once
   in Lean, for every language, under KanonBool (Kanon's Lean library). *)

[@@@lean_root "KanonBool"]

node Bool of bool : TBool
notation Bool
node Not : TBool -> TBool
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem]
node Or : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem]
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]
node Ite : TBool -> a -> a -> a
node Distinct : a list -> TBool
sort TBool

infix "&&" = And, and_
infix "||" = Or, or_
infix "==" = Eq, eq
prefix "not" = Not, not_

constant true = v_true
constant false = v_false
files.bool.kn:
(* The bool module, at the bottom of every language: booleans, equality, [Ite]
   and [Distinct]. The modules above it add their rules to its rule functions
   with [extend rule], and their literals to [sure_neq] with [extend fn].

   Primitives are implemented by hand by each language, in OCaml and in Lean.
   Oracles have no Lean definition: the Lean model is parameterised by them,
   and the properties that the proofs rely on are stated with the language.
   Here, they are the hash-consing order. *)

(* {1 Primitives} *)

(* Sorts terms along the hash-consing order. *)
oracle sort_by_tag : t list -> t list

prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

(* {1 Helpers} *)

fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false

(* whether [a] and [b] surely have different values: the modules above add
   their literals *)
fn sure_neq (a b : t) : bool [@extensible] =
  match (a, b) with
  | _ when not (type_of a = type_of b) -> true
  | Bool a, Bool b -> not (a = b)
  | _ -> false

fn at_most_one (l : t list) : bool =
  match l with [] | [ _ ] -> true | _ -> false

(* {1 Rules} *)

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | false_: false && _ -> v_false
  | true_: true && x -> x
  | not: p && not p -> v_false
  | and_: (a && _ as x) && a -> x
  | or_: (a || _) && a -> a
  | eq_neq: a == x && a == y when sure_neq x y -> v_false

rule or_ : Or (v1, v2) =
  | true_: true || _ -> v_true
  | false_: false || x -> x
  | not: p || not p -> v_true
  | or_: (a || _ as x) || a -> x
  | and_: (a && _) || a -> a

rule not_ : Not sv =
  | true_: true -> v_false
  | false_: false -> v_true
  | not: not sv -> sv
  | or_: v1 || v2 -> not v1 && not v2
  | and_: v1 && v2 -> not v1 || not v2
  | ite: Ite (g, a, b) -> ite g (not a) (not b)
  | distinct: Distinct [ l; r ] -> l == r

rule ite : Ite (guard, if_, else_) =
  | true_: true, _, _ -> if_
  | false_: false, _, _ -> else_
  | bool: _, true, false -> guard
  | not_bool: _, false, true -> not guard
  | false_then: _, false, _ -> not guard && else_
  | true_then: _, true, _ -> guard || else_
  | false_else: _, _, false -> guard && if_
  | true_else: _, _, true -> not guard || if_
  | not_guard: not g, _, _ -> ite g else_ if_
  | guard_then: g, g, _ -> guard || else_
  | guard_else: g, _, g -> guard && if_
  | ite_then: g, Ite (g, x, _), _ -> ite guard x else_
  | ite_else: g, _, Ite (g, _, y) -> ite guard if_ y
  | and_ite_then: g && _, Ite (g, x, _), _ -> ite guard x else_
  | or_ite_else: g || _, _, Ite (g, _, y) -> ite guard if_ y
  | same: _, x, x -> if_

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: v == v -> v_true
  | bools: Bool b1 == Bool b2 -> of_bool (b1 = b2)
  (* distributing over a shared guard lets the branches cancel pairwise *)
  | ite_ite: Ite (b, l, r) == Ite (b, l', r') -> ite b (l == l') (r == r')
  | false_: false == x -> not x
  | true_: true == x -> x
  | nots: not b == not c -> b == c

(* The equality of terms that may have different sorts, false when they do:
   [@untyped], so its operands are not asserted to have the same sort. *)
rule eq_untyped : Eq (v1, v2) [@untyped] =
  | ill_typed: _ when not (type_of v1 = type_of v2) -> v_false
  | typed: _ -> v1 == v2

(* [distinct_check_one a rest] and [distinct_check l] go through the pairs of
   elements in order, and stop at the first pair that is equal ([Some false])
   or not surely different ([None]). *)
fn distinct_check_one (a : t) (rest : t list) : bool option =
  match rest with
  | [] -> Some true
  | b :: rest ->
      if a = b then Some false
      else if sure_neq a b then distinct_check_one a rest
      else None

fn distinct_check (l : t list) : bool option =
  match l with
  | [] -> Some true
  | a :: rest -> (
      match distinct_check_one a rest with
      | Some true -> distinct_check rest
      | r -> r)

rule distinct : Distinct l =
  | small: _ when at_most_one l -> v_true
  | distinct: _ when distinct_check l = Some true -> v_true
  | not_distinct: _ when distinct_check l = Some false -> v_false
  | default: _ -> Distinct (sort_by_tag l)

let node : kind -> ty -> t =
  let module H = Ephemeron.K1.Make (struct
    type nonrec t = t
    let equal a b = equal_kind a.kind b.kind && equal_ty a.ty b.ty
    let hash a = hash_combine (hash_kind a.kind) (hash_ty a.ty)
  end) in
  let table = H.create 1024 and tags = ref 0 in
  fun kind ty ->
    let v = { kind; ty; tag = -1 } in
    match H.find table v with
    | t -> t
    | exception Not_found ->
      let t = { v with tag = !tags } in
      incr tags;
      H.add table t t;
      t

/-- The nodes of the module, over the terms `T` of a language. -/
inductive Node (T : Type) where

  | Not (a1 : T)
  | And (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  | Or (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  | Eq (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  | Ite (a1 : T) (a2 : T) (a3 : T)

namespace Node

variable {T U : Type}

/-- The node with its children mapped by `f`. -/
def map (f : T → U) : Node T → Node U
  | (.Bool x1) => (.Bool x1)
  | (.Not a1) => (.Not (f a1))
  | (.And a1 a2) => (.And (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Or a1 a2) => (.Or (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => (.Eq (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Ite a1 a2 a3) => (.Ite (f a1) (f a2) (f a3))
  | (.Distinct l1) => (.Distinct (l1.map f))

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P`. -/
def All (P : T → Prop) : Node T → Prop
  | (.Bool x1) => True
  | (.Not a1) => P a1
  | (.And a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Or a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Ite a1 a2 a3) => P a1 ∧ P a2 ∧ P a3
  | (.Distinct l1) => (∀ y ∈ l1, P y)

/-- The nodes have the same arguments, and their children are related by `R`. -/
def Rel (R : T → U → Prop) : Node T → Node U → Prop
  | (.Bool x1), (.Bool x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Not a1), (.Not a1') => R a1 a1'
  | (.And a1 a2), (.And a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Or a1 a2), (.Or a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Eq a1 a2), (.Eq a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Ite a1 a2 a3), (.Ite a1' a2' a3') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2' ∧ R a3 a3'
  | (.Distinct l1), (.Distinct l1') => Kanon.Forall₂ R l1 l1'
  | _, _ => False

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/
def children : Node T → List T
  | (.Bool x1) => []
  | (.Not a1) => [a1]
  | (.And a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Or a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Ite a1 a2 a3) => [a1] ++ [a2] ++ [a3]
  | (.Distinct l1) => l1

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P` when all its children do. -/
theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by

  L.node.proj_inj n t

  L.srt.proj_inj s

@[simp] theorem sort_inj_iff {s s' : Srt} : sort (S := S) s = sort s' ↔ s = s' :=
  L.srt.inj_eq_iff

@[simp, kanon_wt] theorem sort_eq_ty {s : Srt} {x : S.Term} : sort s = S.ty x ↔ S.ty x = sort s :=

theorem Node.rel_refines {n n' : Node S.Term} (h : n.Rel S.Refines n') (w : n.All S.WT) :
  n'.All S.WT ∧ (∀ t, Node.wt L.srt.inj S.ty n t → Node.wt L.srt.inj S.ty n' t) ∧
    (n.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c)).Rel Kanon.Sem.FLe (n'.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c)) := by
  cases n <;> cases n' <;> simp only [Node.Rel, Node.All, Node.wt, Node.map] at h w ⊢ <;>
    kanon_rel_refines

    (ht : S.WT (mk n t) → t' = t) : S.Refines (mk n t) (mk n' t') := by
  refine Kanon.Sem.Refines.intro (fun w => ?_) (fun ρ v w _ e => ?_) <;> obtain rfl := (ht w).symm <;>
    rw [WT_mk] at w

class Typed (S : Kanon.Sem) [Lang S] : Prop where
  ev_sort : ∀ ρ e v (s : Srt), S.WT e → S.ty e = sort s → S.ev ρ e = some v →
    Srt.val s v

    {e : S.Term} {s : Srt} (w : S.WT e) (h : S.ty e = sort s) :
  S.ev ρ e = none ∨ ∃ v, S.ev ρ e = some v ∧ Srt.val s v := by
  rcases he : S.ev ρ e with _ | v
  · exact .inl rfl
  · exact .inr ⟨v, rfl, Typed.ev_sort ρ e v s w h he⟩

    bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq_untyped.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_distinct := fun l => KanonBool.Bool.distinct.spec (S := sem) l }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : Kanon.Ops sem) : Kanon.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    bool_sure_neq := Bool.sure_neq O,
    bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step O,
    bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step O,
    bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step O,
    bool_ite := Bool.ite.step O,
    bool_eq := Bool.eq.step O,
    bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step O,
    bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → Kanon.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_not_ := fun sv => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_distinct := fun l => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_orc := h.bool,
      bool_sure_neq := fun a b => KanonBool.Bool.sure_neq.default.ok (S := sem) a b }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_ite := Bool.ite.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq := Bool.eq.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_orc := hO.bool_orc,
      bool_sure_neq := Bool.sure_neq.sound _ hO }

end Kanon

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P` when all its children do. -/
theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by

def opsRaw (orc : Oracle) : BoolExample.Ops sem :=
  { tag_le := orc.tag_le,
    bool_sort_by_tag := orc.bool_sort_by_tag,
    bool_sure_neq := fun a b => KanonBool.Bool.sure_neq.default (S := sem) a b,
    bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.and_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.or_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_not_ := fun sv => KanonBool.Bool.not_.spec (S := sem) sv,
    bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => KanonBool.Bool.ite.spec (S := sem) guard if_ else_,
    bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq_untyped.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_distinct := fun l => KanonBool.Bool.distinct.spec (S := sem) l }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : BoolExample.Ops sem) : BoolExample.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    bool_sure_neq := Bool.sure_neq O,
    bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step O,
    bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step O,
    bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step O,
    bool_ite := Bool.ite.step O,
    bool_eq := Bool.eq.step O,
    bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step O,
    bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → BoolExample.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_not_ := fun sv => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_distinct := fun l => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_orc := h.bool,
      bool_sure_neq := fun a b => KanonBool.Bool.sure_neq.default.ok (S := sem) a b }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_ite := Bool.ite.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq := Bool.eq.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_orc := hO.bool_orc,
      bool_sure_neq := Bool.sure_neq.sound _ hO }

end BoolExample

(* An example language of integers and of arrays of integers: it shows the
   built-in immutable arrays, whose type [int array] is the argument of a node,
   and which rules build, read and update. Its OCaml is tested in test/ocaml,
   and its Lean model and proofs are in lean/: its vec module, without

(* The vec module: integers, and arrays of integers. *)

node Int of int : TInt
notation Int
node Vec of int array : TVec

(** The number of elements of an array. *)
node Len : TVec -> TInt

(** The element at an index, which must be in bounds. *)
node Get : TVec -> TInt -> TInt

(** The array with the element at an index replaced: a copy. *)
node Set : TVec -> TInt -> TInt -> TVec

sort TInt
sort TVec
files.vec.kn:
(* The rules of the vec module. *)

fn in_bounds (a : int array) (i : int) : bool = 0 <= i && i < array_length a

rule len : Len v =
  | lit: Vec a -> Int (array_length a)

rule get : Get (v, i) =
  | lit: Vec a, #k when in_bounds a k -> Int (array_get a k)
  | set_same: Set (_, j, x), k when j = k -> x

rule set : Set (v, i, x) =
  | lit: Vec a, #k, #y when in_bounds a k -> Vec (array_set a k y)

(* arrays are compared structurally *)
fn same (a b : int array) : bool = a = b

(* the conversions between lists and arrays *)
fn of_list (l : int list) : t = Vec (array_of_list l)

fn elements (v : t) : int list =
  match v with
  | Vec a -> array_to_list a
  | _ -> []

namespace ArraysExample.Vec

open Classical Kanon

/-- The sorts of the module. -/
inductive Srt where
  | TInt
  | TVec
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

/-- The nodes of the module, over the terms `T` of a language. -/
inductive Node (T : Type) where
  | Int (x1 : Int)
  | Vec (x1 : (Array Int))
  /-- The number of elements of an array. -/
  | Len (a1 : T)
  /-- The element at an index, which must be in bounds. -/
  | Get (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  /-- The array with the element at an index replaced: a copy. -/
  | Set (a1 : T) (a2 : T) (a3 : T)

namespace Node

variable {T U : Type}

/-- The node with its children mapped by `f`. -/
def map (f : T → U) : Node T → Node U
  | (.Int x1) => (.Int x1)
  | (.Vec x1) => (.Vec x1)
  | (.Len a1) => (.Len (f a1))
  | (.Get a1 a2) => (.Get (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Set a1 a2 a3) => (.Set (f a1) (f a2) (f a3))

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P`. -/
def All (P : T → Prop) : Node T → Prop
  | (.Int x1) => True
  | (.Vec x1) => True
  | (.Len a1) => P a1
  | (.Get a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Set a1 a2 a3) => P a1 ∧ P a2 ∧ P a3

/-- The nodes have the same arguments, and their children are related by `R`. -/
def Rel (R : T → U → Prop) : Node T → Node U → Prop
  | (.Int x1), (.Int x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Vec x1), (.Vec x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Len a1), (.Len a1') => R a1 a1'
  | (.Get a1 a2), (.Get a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Set a1 a2 a3), (.Set a1' a2' a3') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2' ∧ R a3 a3'
  | _, _ => False

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/
def children : Node T → List T
  | (.Int x1) => []
  | (.Vec x1) => []
  | (.Len a1) => [a1]
  | (.Get a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Set a1 a2 a3) => [a1] ++ [a2] ++ [a3]

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P` when all its children do. -/
theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by
  cases n <;> simp [All, children, or_imp, forall_and]

end Node

end ArraysExample.Vec

open Classical Kanon

/-- The typing of the nodes of the module, at the sorts of a language (by the embeddings
of the sorts of the modules), given the types of their children (`ty`). -/
def Node.wt {T Ty : Type} (sVec : ArraysExample.Vec.Srt → Ty) (ty : T → Ty) : Node T → Ty → Prop

  | (.Vec x1), t => (t = (sVec .TVec))
  | (.Len a1), t => (ty a1 = (sVec .TVec) ∧ t = (sVec .TInt))
  | (.Get a1 a2), t => (ty a1 = (sVec .TVec) ∧ ty a2 = (sVec .TInt) ∧ t = (sVec .TInt))
  | (.Set a1 a2 a3), t => (ty a1 = (sVec .TVec) ∧ ty a2 = (sVec .TInt) ∧ ty a3 = (sVec .TInt) ∧ t = (sVec .TVec))

/-- What the module needs of a language `S`: its nodes and sorts embedded in the terms and types
of `S`, which types and evaluates them as the module says. -/
class Lang (S : Kanon.Sem) extends Values S.toDom where
  node : Kanon.NodeEmbed Node S
  srt : Kanon.Embed Srt S.Ty
  WT_inj : ∀ n t, S.WT (node.inj n t) ↔ Node.wt srt.inj S.ty n t ∧ n.All S.WT
  ev_inj : ∀ ρ n t, S.ev ρ (node.inj n t) = Node.eval ρ t (n.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c))
  size_proj : ∀ e n, node.proj e = some n → n.All (fun c => S.size c < S.size e)

@[kanon_wt] theorem WT_mk (n : Node S.Term) (t : S.Ty) :
  S.WT (mk n t) ↔ Node.wt L.srt.inj S.ty n t ∧ n.All S.WT :=
  L.WT_inj n t

  S.ev ρ (mk n t) = Node.eval ρ t (n.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c)) :=
  L.ev_inj ρ n t

@[simp] theorem proj_mk (n : Node S.Term) (t : S.Ty) : proj (mk n t) = some n :=
  L.node.proj_inj n t

@[simp] theorem mk_inj_iff {n n' : Node S.Term} {t t' : S.Ty} :

/-- The sort of the language of a sort of the module. -/
abbrev sort (s : Srt) : S.Ty := L.srt.inj s

/-- The sort of the module that a sort is, if it is one. -/
abbrev sortProj (τ : S.Ty) : Option Srt := L.srt.proj τ

@[simp] theorem sortProj_sort (s : Srt) : sortProj (S := S) (sort s) = some s :=
  L.srt.proj_inj s

@[simp] theorem sort_inj_iff {s s' : Srt} : sort (S := S) s = sort s' ↔ s = s' :=
  L.srt.inj_eq_iff

/-- Equations of sorts, oriented. -/
@[simp, kanon_wt] theorem sort_eq_ty {s : Srt} {x : S.Term} : sort s = S.ty x ↔ S.ty x = sort s :=
  eq_comm

/-- Refined children: the node is typed and evaluated as refined. -/
theorem Node.rel_refines {n n' : Node S.Term} (h : n.Rel S.Refines n') (w : n.All S.WT) :
  n'.All S.WT ∧ (∀ t, Node.wt L.srt.inj S.ty n t → Node.wt L.srt.inj S.ty n' t) ∧
    (n.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c)).Rel Kanon.Sem.FLe (n'.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c)) := by
  cases n <;> cases n' <;> simp only [Node.Rel, Node.All, Node.wt, Node.map] at h w ⊢ <;>
    kanon_rel_refines

/-- Refining the children of a node refines it, at the same sort (when it is well-typed). -/
@[kanon_congr_lemma] theorem mk_congr {n n' : Node S.Term} {t t' : S.Ty} (h : n.Rel S.Refines n')
    (ht : S.WT (mk n t) → t' = t) : S.Refines (mk n t) (mk n' t') := by
  refine Kanon.Sem.Refines.intro (fun w => ?_) (fun ρ v w _ e => ?_) <;> obtain rfl := (ht w).symm <;>
    rw [WT_mk] at w
  · obtain ⟨h1, h2, -⟩ := Node.rel_refines h w.2
    exact ⟨(WT_mk _ _).2 ⟨h2 t w.1, h1⟩, by simp only [ty_mk]⟩
  · rw [ev_mk] at e ⊢
    exact Node.eval_mono ρ t (Node.rel_refines h w.2).2.2 v e

end

attribute [kanon_wt] Node.wt Node.All
attribute [kanon_ev] Node.map Node.eval
attribute [kanon_rel] Node.Rel

/-- The values of the terms of the sorts of the module, in a language `S`: those that the module
gives its sorts (`Srt.val`). Each language proves it. -/
class Typed (S : Kanon.Sem) [Lang S] : Prop where
  ev_sort : ∀ ρ e v (s : Srt), S.WT e → S.ty e = sort s → S.ev ρ e = some v →
    Srt.val s v

/-- The values of a well-typed term of a sort of the module. -/
@[kanon_atom_cases] theorem ev_cases {S : Kanon.Sem} [Lang S] [Typed S] {ρ : S.Env}
    {e : S.Term} {s : Srt} (w : S.WT e) (h : S.ty e = sort s) :
  S.ev ρ e = none ∨ ∃ v, S.ev ρ e = some v ∧ Srt.val s v := by
  rcases he : S.ev ρ e with _ | v
  · exact .inl rfl
  · exact .inr ⟨v, rfl, Typed.ev_sort ρ e v s w h he⟩

attribute [kanon_val] Srt.val

end ArraysExample.Vec

  | (.Int x1) => True
  | (.Vec x1) => True
  | (.Len a1) => a1.WT
  | (.Get a1 a2) => a1.WT ∧ a2.WT
  | (.Set a1 a2 a3) => a1.WT ∧ a2.WT ∧ a3.WT

  | .vec n t => ArraysExample.Vec.Node.eval (D := dom) ρ t (evVec n)

def evVec : ArraysExample.Vec.Node Term → ArraysExample.Vec.Node (Env → Option Val)
  | (.Int x1) => (.Int x1)
  | (.Vec x1) => (.Vec x1)
  | (.Len a1) => (.Len (fun ρ => ev ρ a1))
  | (.Get a1 a2) => (.Get (fun ρ => ev ρ a1) (fun ρ => ev ρ a2))
  | (.Set a1 a2 a3) => (.Set (fun ρ => ev ρ a1) (fun ρ => ev ρ a2) (fun ρ => ev ρ a3))

end

theorem allVec_iff (n : ArraysExample.Vec.Node Term) : allVec n ↔ n.All Term.WT := by
  cases n <;> simp [allVec, ArraysExample.Vec.Node.All]

theorem evVec_eq (n : ArraysExample.Vec.Node Term) : evVec n = n.map (fun c ρ => ev ρ c) := by
  cases n <;> simp only [evVec, ArraysExample.Vec.Node.map]

  Term.WT (.vec n t) ↔ ArraysExample.Vec.Node.wt Ty.vec Term.ty n t ∧ n.All Term.WT := by
  show (_ ∧ allVec n) ↔ _; rw [allVec_iff]

theorem ev_vec (ρ : Env) (n : ArraysExample.Vec.Node Term) (t : Ty) :
  ev ρ (.vec n t) = ArraysExample.Vec.Node.eval (D := dom) ρ t (n.map (fun c ρ => ev ρ c)) :=

      vec_set := Vec.set.step_sound _ hO }

      | _ => none)]).getD

  tag_le : Term → Term → Bool

    Refines (Kanon.Term.Term.add.spec (S := sem) v1 v2) (Term.add.step O v1 v2) := by

  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

def Ext.neg.step (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (v : Term) : Term :=
  (firstSome [Kanon.Ext.Ext.neg.r_neg (S := sem) O.toExtOps v, Kanon.Ext.Ext.neg.r_default (S := sem) O.toExtOps v]).getD
    (Kanon.Ext.Ext.neg.spec (S := sem) v)

theorem Ext.neg.step_sound (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (hO : O.Sound) (v : Term) :
    Refines (Kanon.Ext.Ext.neg.spec (S := sem) v) (Ext.neg.step O v) := by
  unfold Ext.neg.step
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Ext.Ext.neg.r_neg.sound (S := sem) O.toExtOps hO.toExtSound v res h) ?_
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Ext.Ext.neg.r_default.sound (S := sem) O.toExtOps hO.toExtSound v res h) ?_
  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

/-- The rule functions as their specs, without simplification. -/
def opsRaw (orc : Oracle) : Kanon.Ops sem :=
  { tag_le := orc.tag_le,
    term_add := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Term.Term.add.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    ext_neg := fun v => Kanon.Ext.Ext.neg.spec (S := sem) v }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : Kanon.Ops sem) : Kanon.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    term_add := Term.add.step O,
    ext_neg := Ext.neg.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → Kanon.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { term_add := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      ext_neg := fun v => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { term_add := Term.add.step_sound _ hO,
      ext_neg := Ext.neg.step_sound _ hO }

end Kanon

(* A small value language: booleans and mathematical integers, in one module.

[@@@ocaml_prims "Tiny_prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Tiny_rules"]

use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"] [@noeq] [@equal "String.equal"]
  [@hash "Hashtbl.hash"]

(* types of the module Tiny_base, which ocaml-types re-exports *)
type checked [@ocaml "Tiny_base.checked"] = { signed : bool; unsigned : bool }
type rounding [@ocaml "Tiny_base.rounding"] = Nearest | Zero

node Var of var
node Bool of bool
node Int of int : TInt
notation Bool
notation Int
node Not : TBool -> TBool
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true] [@zero false]
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@fold Rules.add] [@unit 0]
node Times : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 1] [@zero 0]
node Lt : TInt -> TInt -> TBool [@fold Rules.lt]
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]
sort TBool
sort TInt

infix "&&" = And, Rules.and_
infix "+" = Plus, Rules.plus
infix "*" = Times, Rules.times
infix "<" = Lt, Rules.lt_
infix "==" = Eq, Rules.eq
prefix "not" = Not, Rules.not_

constant false = Rules.v_false
files.rules.kn:
prim v_true : t
prim v_false : t

fn of_bool (b : bool) : t = if b then v_true else v_false
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y
fn lt (x y : int) : bool = x < y

rule plus : Plus (v1, v2)
rule times : Times (v1, v2)
rule lt_ : Lt (v1, v2)

rule not_ : Not v =
  | lit: true -> v_false
  | not_not: not x -> x

rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not x -> v_false

rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> v_true
  | lits: Int x == Int y -> of_bool (x = y)

(* a parameter of a sort, asserted on entry *)
fn is_zero (v : TInt) : bool =
  match v with
  | 0 -> true
  | _ -> false

(* a node built at a sort *)
fn zero : t = (Int 0 : TInt)

  | (.Bool x1) => (.Bool x1)
  | (.Int x1) => (.Int x1)
  | (.Not a1) => (.Not (f a1))
  | (.And a1 a2) => (.And (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => (.Plus (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Times a1 a2) => (.Times (f a1) (f a2))

  | (.Eq a1 a2) => (.Eq (f a1) (f a2))

  | (.Lt a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2

  | (.Bool x1) => []
  | (.Int x1) => []
  | (.Not a1) => [a1]
  | (.And a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]

  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

def Rules.eq.step (O : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) : Term :=
  (firstSome [Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.r_same (S := sem) O v1 v2, Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.r_lits (S := sem) O v1 v2, Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.r_default (S := sem) O v1 v2]).getD
    (Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.spec (S := sem) v1 v2)

theorem Rules.eq.step_sound (O : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem) (hO : O.Sound) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) :
    Refines (Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.spec (S := sem) v1 v2) (Rules.eq.step O v1 v2) := by
  unfold Rules.eq.step
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.r_same.sound (S := sem) O hO v1 v2 res h) ?_
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.r_lits.sound (S := sem) O hO v1 v2 res h) ?_
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.r_default.sound (S := sem) O hO v1 v2 res h) ?_
  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

/-- The rule functions as their specs, without simplification. -/
def opsRaw (orc : Oracle) : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem :=
  { tag_le := orc.tag_le,
    rules_plus := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Rules.Rules.plus.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    rules_times := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Rules.Rules.times.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    rules_lt_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Rules.Rules.lt_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    rules_not_ := fun v => Kanon.Rules.Rules.not_.spec (S := sem) v,
    rules_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Rules.Rules.and_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    rules_eq := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Rules.Rules.eq.spec (S := sem) v1 v2 }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem) : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    rules_plus := Rules.plus.step O,
    rules_times := Rules.times.step O,
    rules_lt_ := Rules.lt_.step O,
    rules_not_ := Rules.not_.step O,
    rules_and_ := Rules.and_.step O,
    rules_eq := Rules.eq.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → Kanon.Rules.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { rules_plus := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      rules_times := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      rules_lt_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      rules_not_ := fun v => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      rules_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      rules_eq := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { rules_plus := Rules.plus.step_sound _ hO,
      rules_times := Rules.times.step_sound _ hO,
      rules_lt_ := Rules.lt_.step_sound _ hO,
      rules_not_ := Rules.not_.step_sound _ hO,
      rules_and_ := Rules.and_.step_sound _ hO,
      rules_eq := Rules.eq.step_sound _ hO }

end Kanon

namespace Kanon

/-- The nodes of the module, over the terms `T` of a language. -/
inductive Node (T : Type) where
  | Var (x1 : Int)
  | Xor (a1 : T) (a2 : T)

namespace Node

variable {T U : Type}

/-- The node with its children mapped by `f`. -/
def map (f : T → U) : Node T → Node U
  | (.Var x1) => (.Var x1)
  | (.Xor a1 a2) => (.Xor (f a1) (f a2))

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P`. -/
def All (P : T → Prop) : Node T → Prop
  | (.Var x1) => True
  | (.Xor a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2

/-- The nodes have the same arguments, and their children are related by `R`. -/
def Rel (R : T → U → Prop) : Node T → Node U → Prop
  | (.Var x1), (.Var x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Xor a1 a2), (.Xor a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | _, _ => False

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/
def children : Node T → List T
  | (.Var x1) => []
  | (.Xor a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P` when all its children do. -/
theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by
  cases n <;> simp [All, children, or_imp, forall_and]

end Node

end Kanon

/-- The rule functions as their specs, without simplification. -/
def opsRaw (orc : Oracle) : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem :=
  { tag_le := orc.tag_le,
    bool_sort_by_tag := orc.bool_sort_by_tag,
    bool_sure_neq := fun a b => KanonBool.Bool.sure_neq.default (S := sem) a b,
    bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.and_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.or_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_not_ := fun sv => KanonBool.Bool.not_.spec (S := sem) sv,
    bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => KanonBool.Bool.ite.spec (S := sem) guard if_ else_,
    bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq_untyped.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_distinct := fun l => KanonBool.Bool.distinct.spec (S := sem) l,
    rules_xor := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Rules.Rules.xor.spec (S := sem) v1 v2 }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem) : Kanon.Rules.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    bool_sure_neq := Bool.sure_neq O,
    bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step O,
    bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step O,
    bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step O,
    bool_ite := Bool.ite.step O,
    bool_eq := Bool.eq.step O,
    bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step O,
    bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step O,
    rules_xor := Rules.xor.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → Kanon.Rules.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_not_ := fun sv => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_distinct := fun l => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      rules_xor := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_orc := h.bool,
      bool_sure_neq := fun a b => KanonBool.Bool.sure_neq.default.ok (S := sem) a b }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_ite := Bool.ite.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq := Bool.eq.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step_sound _ hO,
      rules_xor := Rules.xor.step_sound _ hO,
      bool_orc := hO.bool_orc,
      bool_sure_neq := Bool.sure_neq.sound _ hO }

end Kanon

[@@@warning "-a"]

type var = string

and kind =
  | Var of var (** A variable. *)
  | Bool of bool (** A boolean literal. *)
  | Int of Z.t (** An integer literal. *)
  | Op1 of op1 * t
  | Op2 of op2 * t * t

and op1 =
  | Not (** Negation. *)

and op2 =
  | And (** Conjunction. *)
  | Plus (** The sum of two integers. *)
  | Eq (** Equality of two terms of any sort. *)

and ty =
  | TBool (** The sort of booleans. *)
  | TInt (** The sort of integers. *)

and t = {
  kind : kind;
  ty : ty;
  tag : int;
}

let hash_combine x y = (x * 65599) + y

let rec equal_t (a : t) (b : t) = Int.equal a.tag b.tag

and hash_t (a : t) = a.tag

and equal_var (a : var) (b : var) = Stdlib.( = ) a b

and hash_var (a : var) = Hashtbl.hash a

and equal_kind (a : kind) (b : kind) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Var a1, Var b1 -> equal_var a1 b1
  | Bool a1, Bool b1 -> Stdlib.Bool.equal a1 b1
  | Int a1, Int b1 -> Z.equal a1 b1
  | Op1 (a1, a2), Op1 (b1, b2) -> equal_op1 a1 b1 && equal_t a2 b2
  | Op2 (a1, a2, a3), Op2 (b1, b2, b3) ->
      equal_op2 a1 b1 && equal_t a2 b2 && equal_t a3 b3
  | _ -> false

and hash_kind (a : kind) =
  match a with
  | Var a1 -> hash_combine (0) (hash_var a1)
  | Bool a1 -> hash_combine (1) (Stdlib.Bool.to_int a1)
  | Int a1 -> hash_combine (2) (Z.hash a1)
  | Op1 (a1, a2) -> hash_combine (hash_combine (3) (hash_op1 a1)) (hash_t a2)
  | Op2 (a1, a2, a3) ->
      hash_combine
        (hash_combine (hash_combine (4) (hash_op2 a1)) (hash_t a2))
        (hash_t a3)

and equal_op1 (a : op1) (b : op1) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Not, Not -> true

and hash_op1 (a : op1) =
  match a with
  | Not -> 0

and equal_op2 (a : op2) (b : op2) =
  match (a, b) with
  | And, And -> true
  | Plus, Plus -> true
  | Eq, Eq -> true
  | _ -> false

and hash_op2 (a : op2) =
  match a with
  | And -> 0
  | Plus -> 1
  | Eq -> 2

and equal_ty (a : ty) (b : ty) =
  match (a, b) with
  | TBool, TBool -> true
  | TInt, TInt -> true
  | _ -> false

and hash_ty (a : ty) =
  match a with
  | TBool -> 0
  | TInt -> 1

(* Not safe across domains (TODO). *)
let node : kind -> ty -> t =
  let module H = Ephemeron.K1.Make (struct
    type nonrec t = t
    let equal a b = equal_kind a.kind b.kind && equal_ty a.ty b.ty
    let hash a = hash_combine (hash_kind a.kind) (hash_ty a.ty)
  end) in
  let table = H.create 1024 and tags = ref 0 in
  fun kind ty ->
    let v = { kind; ty; tag = -1 } in
    match H.find table v with
    | t -> t
    | exception Not_found ->
      let t = { v with tag = !tags } in
      incr tags;
      H.add table t t;
      t

  | And (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  /-- The sum of two integers. -/
  | Plus (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  /-- Equality of two terms of any sort. -/

namespace Node

variable {T U : Type}

/-- The node with its children mapped by `f`. -/
def map (f : T → U) : Node T → Node U
  | (.Var x1) => (.Var x1)
  | (.Bool x1) => (.Bool x1)
  | (.Int x1) => (.Int x1)
  | (.Not a1) => (.Not (f a1))
  | (.And a1 a2) => (.And (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => (.Plus (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => (.Eq (f a1) (f a2))

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P`. -/
def All (P : T → Prop) : Node T → Prop
  | (.Var x1) => True
  | (.Bool x1) => True
  | (.Int x1) => True
  | (.Not a1) => P a1
  | (.And a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2

/-- The nodes have the same arguments, and their children are related by `R`. -/
def Rel (R : T → U → Prop) : Node T → Node U → Prop
  | (.Var x1), (.Var x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Bool x1), (.Bool x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Int x1), (.Int x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Not a1), (.Not a1') => R a1 a1'
  | (.And a1 a2), (.And a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Plus a1 a2), (.Plus a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Eq a1 a2), (.Eq a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | _, _ => False

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/
def children : Node T → List T
  | (.Var x1) => []
  | (.Bool x1) => []
  | (.Int x1) => []
  | (.Not a1) => [a1]
  | (.And a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P` when all its children do. -/
theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by
  cases n <;> simp [All, children, or_imp, forall_and]

def Node.wt {T Ty : Type} (sLang : Kanon.Srt → Ty) (ty : T → Ty) : Node T → Ty → Prop

  | (.Bool x1), t => (t = (sLang .TBool))

  | (.Not a1), t => (ty a1 = (sLang .TBool) ∧ t = (sLang .TBool))
  | (.And a1 a2), t => (ty a1 = (sLang .TBool) ∧ ty a2 = (sLang .TBool) ∧ t = (sLang .TBool))
  | (.Plus a1 a2), t => (ty a1 = (sLang .TInt) ∧ ty a2 = (sLang .TInt) ∧ t = (sLang .TInt))
  | (.Eq a1 a2), t => (ty a2 = ty a1 ∧ t = (sLang .TBool))

/-- What the module needs of a language `S`: its nodes and sorts embedded in the terms and types
of `S`, which types and evaluates them as the module says. -/
class Lang (S : Kanon.Sem) extends Values S.toDom where
  node : Kanon.NodeEmbed Node S
  srt : Kanon.Embed Srt S.Ty
  WT_inj : ∀ n t, S.WT (node.inj n t) ↔ Node.wt srt.inj S.ty n t ∧ n.All S.WT
  ev_inj : ∀ ρ n t, S.ev ρ (node.inj n t) = Node.eval ρ t (n.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c))

abbrev mk (n : Node S.Term) (t : S.Ty) : S.Term := L.node.inj n t

/-- The node of the module that a term is, if it is one. -/

@[simp, kanon_wt] theorem ty_mk (n : Node S.Term) (t : S.Ty) : S.ty (mk n t) = t :=
  L.node.ty_inj n t

@[kanon_wt] theorem WT_mk (n : Node S.Term) (t : S.Ty) :
  S.WT (mk n t) ↔ Node.wt L.srt.inj S.ty n t ∧ n.All S.WT :=
  L.WT_inj n t

@[kanon_ev] theorem ev_mk (ρ : S.Env) (n : Node S.Term) (t : S.Ty) :
  S.ev ρ (mk n t) = Node.eval ρ t (n.map (fun c ρ => S.ev ρ c)) :=

  L.node.proj_inj n t

and hash_t (a : t) = a.tag

  match a with
  | Var a1 -> hash_combine (0) (hash_var a1)
  | Bool a1 -> hash_combine (1) (Stdlib.Bool.to_int a1)
  | Int a1 -> hash_combine (2) (Z.hash a1)

  | Op2 (a1, a2, a3) ->

        (hash_t a3)

and equal_op1 (a : op1) (b : op1) =
  match (a, b) with
  | Not, Not -> true

and hash_op1 (a : op1) =
  match a with
  | Not -> 0

and equal_op2 (a : op2) (b : op2) =
  match (a, b) with
  | And, And -> true
  | Plus, Plus -> true
  | Eq, Eq -> true
  | _ -> false

and hash_op2 (a : op2) =

  | And -> 0
  | Plus -> 1
  | Eq -> 2

and equal_ty (a : ty) (b : ty) =
  match (a, b) with
  | TBool, TBool -> true
  | TInt, TInt -> true
  | _ -> false

and hash_ty (a : ty) =

  | TInt -> 1

  | (.Eq a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2

  | (.Bool x1), (.Bool x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Int x1), (.Int x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Not a1), (.Not a1') => R a1 a1'
  | (.And a1 a2), (.And a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Plus a1 a2), (.Plus a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'

  | (.Int x1) => []
  | (.Not a1) => [a1]

/-- The rule functions, oracles and extensible helpers of the module, in the model of a
language. -/
structure Ops (S : Kanon.Sem) extends toLangOps : Kanon.Ops S where
  rules_not_ : S.Term → S.Term
  rules_and_ : S.Term → S.Term → S.Term
  rules_plus : S.Term → S.Term → S.Term
  rules_eq : S.Term → S.Term → S.Term

variable {S : Kanon.Sem} [Kanon.Lang S]

/-- Negation of a boolean. -/
def Rules.negb (b : Bool) : Bool :=
  (! b)

/-- Sum of two integers. -/
def Rules.add (x : Int) (y : Int) : Int :=
  (x + y)

attribute [kanon_body] Rules.negb Rules.add

def Rules.not_.spec (v : S.Term) : S.Term :=
  (Kanon.mk (.Not v) (Kanon.sort .TBool))

def Rules.and_.spec (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : S.Term :=
  (Kanon.mk (.And v1 v2) (Kanon.sort .TBool))

def Rules.plus.spec (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : S.Term :=
  (Kanon.mk (.Plus v1 v2) (Kanon.sort .TInt))

def Rules.eq.spec (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : S.Term :=
  (Kanon.mk (.Eq v1 v2) (Kanon.sort .TBool))

attribute [kanon_spec]
  Rules.not_.spec
  Rules.and_.spec
  Rules.plus.spec
  Rules.eq.spec

def Rules.not_.r_lit (O : Ops S) (v : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match (Kanon.proj v) with
    | some (.Bool b) =>
    (whenSome true
    ((Kanon.mk (.Bool (Kanon.Rules.Rules.negb b)) (Kanon.sort .TBool))))
    | _ => none)

def Rules.not_.r_not (O : Ops S) (v : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match (Kanon.proj v) with
    | some (.Not x) =>
    (whenSome true (x))
    | _ => none)

def Rules.not_.r_default (O : Ops S) (v : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v with
    | _ =>
    (whenSome true ((Kanon.mk (.Not v) (Kanon.sort .TBool)))))

def Rules.and_.r_unit_true (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v1, (Kanon.proj v2) with
    | x, some (.Bool true) =>
    (whenSome true (x))
    | _, _ => none)
  <|> (match (Kanon.proj v1), v2 with
        | some (.Bool true), x =>
        (whenSome true (x))
        | _, _ => none)

def Rules.and_.r_zero_false (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v1, (Kanon.proj v2) with
    | _, some (.Bool false) =>
    (whenSome true ((Kanon.mk (.Bool false) (Kanon.sort .TBool))))
    | _, _ => none)
  <|> (match (Kanon.proj v1), v2 with
        | some (.Bool false), _ =>
        (whenSome true ((Kanon.mk (.Bool false) (Kanon.sort .TBool))))
        | _, _ => none)

def Rules.and_.r_same (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v1, v2 with | v, kanon__2 => (whenSome (decide (v = kanon__2)) (v)))

def Rules.and_.r_default (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v1, v2 with
    | _, _ =>
    (whenSome true
    ((if O.tag_le v1 v2
     then (Kanon.mk (.And v1 v2) (Kanon.sort .TBool))
     else (Kanon.mk (.And v2 v1) (Kanon.sort .TBool))))))

def Rules.plus.r_lits (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match (Kanon.proj v1), (Kanon.proj v2) with
    | some (.Int i1), some (.Int i2) =>
    (whenSome true
    ((Kanon.mk (.Int (Kanon.Rules.Rules.add i1 i2)) (Kanon.sort .TInt))))
    | _, _ => none)

def Rules.plus.r_unit_zero (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v1, (Kanon.proj v2) with
    | x, some (.Int kanon__2) =>
    (whenSome (decide (kanon__2 = (0 : Int))) (x))
    | _, _ => none)
  <|> (match (Kanon.proj v1), v2 with
        | some (.Int kanon__2), x =>
        (whenSome (decide (kanon__2 = (0 : Int))) (x))
        | _, _ => none)

def Rules.plus.r_default (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v1, v2 with
    | _, _ =>
    (whenSome true
    ((if O.tag_le v1 v2
     then (Kanon.mk (.Plus v1 v2) (Kanon.sort .TInt))
     else (Kanon.mk (.Plus v2 v1) (Kanon.sort .TInt))))))

def Rules.eq.r_default (O : Ops S) (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term) : Option S.Term :=
  (match v1, v2 with
    | _, _ =>
    (whenSome true
    ((if O.tag_le v1 v2
     then (Kanon.mk (.Eq v1 v2) (Kanon.sort .TBool))
     else (Kanon.mk (.Eq v2 v1) (Kanon.sort .TBool))))))

/-- What the proofs assume of the model: its rule functions refine their specs, its oracles
and extensible helpers do what they are assumed to do. -/
structure Ops.Sound (O : Ops S) : Prop extends toLangSound : Kanon.Ops.Sound O.toLangOps where
  rules_not_ : ∀ (v : S.Term), S.Refines (Rules.not_.spec v) (O.rules_not_ v)
  rules_and_ : ∀ (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term), S.Refines (Rules.and_.spec v1 v2) (O.rules_and_ v1 v2)
  rules_plus : ∀ (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term), S.Refines (Rules.plus.spec v1 v2) (O.rules_plus v1 v2)
  rules_eq : ∀ (v1 : S.Term) (v2 : S.Term), S.Refines (Rules.eq.spec v1 v2) (O.rules_eq v1 v2)

end Kanon.Rules

(* A tiny value language: booleans and integers. *)

[@@@ocaml_prims "Prims"]
[@@@ocaml_rules "Rules"]

use "rules"

type var [@ocaml "string"] [@lean "String"]

(** A variable. *)
node Var of var
(** A boolean literal. *)
node Bool of bool : TBool
(** An integer literal. *)
node Int of int : TInt
(** Negation. *)
node Not : TBool -> TBool [@invol] [@fold Rules.negb]
(** Conjunction. *)
node And : TBool -> TBool -> TBool [@comm] [@idem] [@unit true] [@zero false]
(** The sum of two integers. *)
node Plus : TInt -> TInt -> TInt [@comm] [@unit 0] [@fold Rules.add]
(** Equality of two terms of any sort. *)
node Eq : a -> a -> TBool [@comm]

(** The sort of booleans. *)
sort TBool
(** The sort of integers. *)
sort TInt

notation Bool
notation Int

infix "&&" = And, Rules.and_
infix "+" = Plus, Rules.plus
infix "==" = Eq, Rules.eq
prefix "not" = Not, Rules.not_
files.rules.kn:
(** Whether a variable is surely a natural number. *)
prim var_is_nat : var -> bool

(* Helpers *)
fn negb (b : bool) : bool = not b
fn add (x y : int) : int = x + y

(** Whether a term is surely a natural number. *)
fn is_nat (v : t) : bool =
  match v with
  | Int n -> n >= 0
  | Var x -> var_is_nat x
  | l + r -> is_nat l && is_nat r
  | _ -> false

(** A size estimate, for the OCaml code around the simplifier: not modelled in Lean. *)
fn cost (v : t) : int [@no_lean] =
  match v with
  | l + r -> cost l + cost r + 1
  | _ -> 1

(* Rule functions: the rules derived from the laws of their spec come first,
   then these. *)

rule not_ : Not v

(** Conjunction. *)
rule and_ : And (v1, v2) =
  | not_: x && not x -> Bool false

(** Sum: adjacent literals are added. *)
rule plus : Plus (v1, v2) =
  | assoc: (x + #a) + #b -> x + Int (a + b)

(** Equality: literals are compared, and a negative literal differs from a natural number. *)
rule eq : Eq (v1, v2) =
  | same: x == x -> Bool true
  | lits: Int x == Int y -> Bool (x = y)
  | true_: true == x -> x
  | neg: Int x == y when x < 0 && is_nat y -> Bool false

variable {T U : Type}

/-- The node with its children mapped by `f`. -/
def map (f : T → U) : Node T → Node U
  | (.Var x1) => (.Var x1)
  | (.Bool x1) => (.Bool x1)
  | (.Int x1) => (.Int x1)
  | (.Not a1) => (.Not (f a1))
  | (.And a1 a2) => (.And (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => (.Plus (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => (.Eq (f a1) (f a2))

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P`. -/
def All (P : T → Prop) : Node T → Prop
  | (.Var x1) => True
  | (.Bool x1) => True
  | (.Int x1) => True
  | (.Not a1) => P a1
  | (.And a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2

/-- The nodes have the same arguments, and their children are related by `R`. -/
def Rel (R : T → U → Prop) : Node T → Node U → Prop
  | (.Var x1), (.Var x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Bool x1), (.Bool x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Int x1), (.Int x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Not a1), (.Not a1') => R a1 a1'
  | (.And a1 a2), (.And a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Plus a1 a2), (.Plus a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Eq a1 a2), (.Eq a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/
def children : Node T → List T
  | (.Var x1) => []
  | (.Bool x1) => []
  | (.Int x1) => []
  | (.Not a1) => [a1]
  | (.And a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Eq a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]

theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by

/-- The rule functions as their specs, without simplification. -/
def opsRaw (orc : Oracle) : IntsExample.Ops sem :=
  { tag_le := orc.tag_le,
    bool_sort_by_tag := orc.bool_sort_by_tag,
    bool_sure_neq := fun a b => KanonBool.Bool.sure_neq.default (S := sem) a b,
    bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.and_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.or_.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_not_ := fun sv => KanonBool.Bool.not_.spec (S := sem) sv,
    bool_ite := fun guard if_ else_ => KanonBool.Bool.ite.spec (S := sem) guard if_ else_,
    bool_eq := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_eq_untyped := fun v1 v2 => KanonBool.Bool.eq_untyped.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    bool_distinct := fun l => KanonBool.Bool.distinct.spec (S := sem) l,
    int_plus := fun v1 v2 => IntMod.Int.plus.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    int_int_lt := fun v1 v2 => IntMod.Int.int_lt.spec (S := sem) v1 v2 }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : IntsExample.Ops sem) : IntsExample.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    bool_sure_neq := Bool.sure_neq O,
    bool_and_ := Bool.and_.step O,
    bool_or_ := Bool.or_.step O,
    bool_not_ := Bool.not_.step O,
    bool_ite := Bool.ite.step O,
    bool_eq := Bool.eq.step O,
    bool_eq_untyped := Bool.eq_untyped.step O,
    bool_distinct := Bool.distinct.step O,
    int_plus := Int.plus.step O,
    int_int_lt := Int.int_lt.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → IntsExample.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { bool_and_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_or_ := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      bool_not_ := fun sv => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,

  | TInt
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

inductive Node (T : Type) where
  /-- An integer literal. -/
  | Int (x1 : Int)
  /-- The sum of two integers. -/
  | Plus (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  /-- The quotient: the divisor is known to be non-zero. -/
  | Div (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  /-- The square of an integer plus one, which is not zero. -/
  | Sq1 (a1 : T)

variable {T U : Type}

/-- The node with its children mapped by `f`. -/
def map (f : T → U) : Node T → Node U
  | (.Int x1) => (.Int x1)
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => (.Plus (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Div a1 a2) => (.Div (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Sq1 a1) => (.Sq1 (f a1))

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P`. -/
def All (P : T → Prop) : Node T → Prop
  | (.Int x1) => True
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Div a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Sq1 a1) => P a1

/-- The nodes have the same arguments, and their children are related by `R`. -/
def Rel (R : T → U → Prop) : Node T → Node U → Prop
  | (.Int x1), (.Int x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Plus a1 a2), (.Plus a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Div a1 a2), (.Div a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Sq1 a1), (.Sq1 a1') => R a1 a1'
  | _, _ => False

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/
def children : Node T → List T
  | (.Int x1) => []
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Div a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Sq1 a1) => [a1]

theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by
  cases n <;> simp [All, children, or_imp, forall_and]

    (Kanon.Int.Int.div.spec (S := sem) v1 v2)

theorem Int.div.step_sound (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (hO : O.Sound) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) (hs_v2 : Kanon.Int.Nonzero (S := sem) v2) :
    Refines (Kanon.Int.Int.div.spec (S := sem) v1 v2) (Int.div.step O v1 v2) := by
  unfold Int.div.step
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Int.Int.div.r_self.sound (S := sem) O.toIntOps hO.toIntSound v1 v2 hs_v2 res h) ?_
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Int.Int.div.r_default.sound (S := sem) O.toIntOps hO.toIntSound v1 v2 hs_v2 res h) ?_
  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

def Int.sq1.step (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (v : Term) : Term :=
  (firstSome [Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.r_default (S := sem) O.toIntOps v]).getD
    (Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.spec (S := sem) v)

theorem Int.sq1.step_sound (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (hO : O.Sound) (v : Term) :
    Refines (Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.spec (S := sem) v) (Int.sq1.step O v) := by
  unfold Int.sq1.step
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.r_default.sound (S := sem) O.toIntOps hO.toIntSound v res h) ?_
  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

theorem Int.sq1.step_post (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (hO : O.Sound) (v : Term) :
    Kanon.Int.Nonzero (S := sem) (Int.sq1.step O v) := by
  unfold Int.sq1.step
  refine Kanon.getD_firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.r_default.post_sound (S := sem) O.toIntOps hO.toIntSound v res h) ?_
  exact Kanon.getD_firstSome_nil (Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.spec_post.ok (S := sem) v)

/-- The rule functions as their specs, without simplification. -/
def opsRaw (orc : Oracle) : Kanon.Ops sem :=
  { tag_le := orc.tag_le,
    int_plus := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Int.Int.plus.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    int_div := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Int.Int.div.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    int_sq1 := fun v => Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.spec (S := sem) v }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : Kanon.Ops sem) : Kanon.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    int_plus := Int.plus.step O,
    int_div := Int.div.step O,
    int_sq1 := Int.sq1.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → Kanon.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { int_plus := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      int_div := fun v1 v2 hs_v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      int_sq1 := fun v => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      int_sq1_post := fun v => Kanon.Int.Int.sq1.spec_post.ok (S := sem) v }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { int_plus := Int.plus.step_sound _ hO,
      int_div := Int.div.step_sound _ hO,
      int_sq1 := Int.sq1.step_sound _ hO,
      int_sq1_post := Int.sq1.step_post _ hO }

end Kanon

namespace Kanon.Int

open Classical Kanon

/-- The sorts of the module. -/
inductive Srt where
  /-- The sort of integers. -/
  | TInt
  /-- The sort of the results of a comparison. -/
  | TBool
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

/-- The nodes of the module, over the terms `T` of a language. -/
inductive Node (T : Type) where
  /-- An integer literal. -/
  | Int (x1 : Int)
  /-- The sum of two integers. -/
  | Plus (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  /-- The quotient: the divisor is known to be non-zero. -/
  | Div (a1 : T) (a2 : T)
  /-- The order on integers. -/
  | Lt (a1 : T) (a2 : T)

namespace Node

variable {T U : Type}

/-- The node with its children mapped by `f`. -/
def map (f : T → U) : Node T → Node U
  | (.Int x1) => (.Int x1)
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => (.Plus (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Div a1 a2) => (.Div (f a1) (f a2))
  | (.Lt a1 a2) => (.Lt (f a1) (f a2))

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P`. -/
def All (P : T → Prop) : Node T → Prop
  | (.Int x1) => True
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Div a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2
  | (.Lt a1 a2) => P a1 ∧ P a2

/-- The nodes have the same arguments, and their children are related by `R`. -/
def Rel (R : T → U → Prop) : Node T → Node U → Prop
  | (.Int x1), (.Int x1') => x1 = x1'
  | (.Plus a1 a2), (.Plus a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Div a1 a2), (.Div a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | (.Lt a1 a2), (.Lt a1' a2') => R a1 a1' ∧ R a2 a2'
  | _, _ => False

/-- The children of the node, in order. -/
def children : Node T → List T
  | (.Int x1) => []
  | (.Plus a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Div a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]
  | (.Lt a1 a2) => [a1] ++ [a2]

/-- Every child of the node satisfies `P` when all its children do. -/
theorem all_iff (P : T → Prop) (n : Node T) : n.All P ↔ ∀ c ∈ n.children, P c := by
  cases n <;> simp [All, children, or_imp, forall_and]

end Node

end Kanon.Int

def Int.div.step (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) : Term :=
  (firstSome [Kanon.Int.Int.div.r_default (S := sem) O.toIntOps v1 v2]).getD
    (Kanon.Int.Int.div.spec (S := sem) v1 v2)

theorem Int.div.step_sound (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (hO : O.Sound) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) :
    Refines (Kanon.Int.Int.div.spec (S := sem) v1 v2) (Int.div.step O v1 v2) := by
  unfold Int.div.step
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Int.Int.div.r_default.sound (S := sem) O.toIntOps hO.toIntSound v1 v2 res h) ?_
  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

def Int.int_lt.step (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) : Term :=
  (firstSome [Kanon.Int.Int.int_lt.r_default (S := sem) O.toIntOps v1 v2]).getD
    (Kanon.Int.Int.int_lt.spec (S := sem) v1 v2)

theorem Int.int_lt.step_sound (O : Kanon.Ops sem) (hO : O.Sound) (v1 : Term) (v2 : Term) :
    Refines (Kanon.Int.Int.int_lt.spec (S := sem) v1 v2) (Int.int_lt.step O v1 v2) := by
  unfold Int.int_lt.step
  refine Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_cons (fun res h => Kanon.Int.Int.int_lt.r_default.sound (S := sem) O.toIntOps hO.toIntSound v1 v2 res h) ?_
  exact Kanon.Refinement.firstSome_nil

/-- The rule functions as their specs, without simplification. -/
def opsRaw (orc : Oracle) : Kanon.Ops sem :=
  { tag_le := orc.tag_le,
    int_plus := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Int.Int.plus.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    int_div := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Int.Int.div.spec (S := sem) v1 v2,
    int_int_lt := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Int.Int.int_lt.spec (S := sem) v1 v2 }

/-- One step of the rule functions, over those of `O`. -/
def opsStep (O : Kanon.Ops sem) : Kanon.Ops sem :=
  { O with
    int_plus := Int.plus.step O,
    int_div := Int.div.step O,
    int_int_lt := Int.int_lt.step O }

/-- The rule functions, with `n` steps of fuel. -/
def opsN (orc : Oracle) : Nat → Kanon.Ops sem
  | 0 => opsRaw orc
  | n + 1 => opsStep (opsN orc n)

/-- Every rule function refines its spec, for any amount of fuel. -/
theorem opsN_sound (orc : Oracle) (h : orc.Compat) : ∀ n, (opsN orc n).Sound
  | 0 =>
    { int_plus := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      int_div := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl,
      int_int_lt := fun v1 v2 => Kanon.Sem.Refines.refl }
  | n + 1 =>
    have hO := opsN_sound orc h n
    { int_plus := Int.plus.step_sound _ hO,
      int_div := Int.div.step_sound _ hO,
      int_int_lt := Int.int_lt.step_sound _ hO }

end Kanon
